title: vllm-project/vllm: serve an open model behind an API you run
friendlyTitle: vLLM: run an open model as an API on your own hardware
summary: vLLM is the widely used open-source engine for serving language models, with about 94,400 stars and another 98 today on GitHub's Python trending list. It offers an OpenAI-compatible API, continuous batching, quantization, and tool calling, and it runs on Nvidia, AMD, and a long list of other accelerators, including TPUs. DeepSeek says its new DeepInfer framework was originally built primarily on vLLM.
friendlySummary: vLLM is a widely used open-source engine for serving language models. It has about 94,400 stars, and it gained another 98 today on GitHub's Python trending list. It offers an API that looks like OpenAI's, plus batching, smaller-number formats, and tool calling. It runs on Nvidia, AMD, and many other chips, including Google TPUs. DeepSeek says its new DeepInfer framework started from vLLM.
whyItMatters: Use it when you want a model from Hugging Face to answer as an API on hardware you control, instead of sending every request to a closed lab. It is the default serving path for a lot of open models, and the reference point for the DeepSeek stack released today.
